# Noisy Readout Depth

Question: how does coherent terminal readout depth constrain local phase information under independent detector noise?

Authoritative route:
- science/model.md: exact model, depth convention, quantifiers, and T1–T4.
- science/converse.md: erasure degradation, environmental gauge, support-intersection covariance, and causal-cone counts.
- science/construction.md: inherited compress–Hadamard–fanout primitive organized into blocks; exact parity likelihood; two-setting and continuous-phase variants; depth and gate count.
- science/frontier.md: finite grouping lemma, full-cube tiling, uniform-in-size logarithmic lattice frontier, and all-to-all bounds.
- science/detectors.md: fixed finite-alphabet classical detectors, overlap, repetition discrimination, and independent random-complement symmetrization.
- science/interpretation.md: resource accounting, global phase ambiguity, and counterexamples outside the model.
- references/RELATED_WORK.md: inherited methods, exact model/quantifier comparison, and source locations.
- references/references.bib: structured bibliographic metadata.
- learning/README.md: entrypoint for the common learning route and its two phases.
- learning/MILESTONES.md: exactly 30 project-defined understanding targets, dependencies, and science pointers; M01–M12 background, M13–M30 narrative.
- learning/ANCHOR.md: the single educational anchor, Tóth and Apellaniz (2014), arXiv:1405.4878v4; selected sections and translated notation.
- learning/BRIDGE.md: original explanation connecting the anchor to terminal detector noise, block decoding, the converse, and the depth frontier.
- verification/README.md: reproduction commands and the scope of finite checks.

For the shortest scientific story, read README.md, science/model.md, and science/interpretation.md.
For a proof audit, read model, converse, construction, frontier, then detectors.
For study, start with learning/README.md, use learning/MILESTONES.md as the fixed project map, and follow learning/ANCHOR.md and learning/BRIDGE.md alongside the linked science pages.
For reproduction, run python3 verification/run_all.py after installing verification/requirements.txt.

Essential distinctions:
- N qubit sensors, additive generator sum(Z_i)/2; arbitrary supplied input state.
- d counts disjoint two-qubit layers after encoding, with ideal gates and one independent terminal detector round.
- The converse is pointwise and applies to every probe; the lower protocol works at every phase with a retained setting label.
- Full cubic grids support matched geometric achievability. Bounded density alone supports only the geometric converse.
- The lattice result matches the order of log(1+F/N). All-to-all has a matching Heisenberg-depth order but an unresolved leading coefficient.
- Continuous recorded phases attain an asymptotically unit ideal-information fraction; two fixed settings suffice for a constant fraction.
- The asymmetric-detector BSC formula is exact after unmasking and marginalizing complement labels; retaining more data may increase information.
- Local Fisher information, even uniformly over phase, does not resolve global phase aliases.
- Readout depth is not total preparation-and-sensing cost.
- Purification machinery and the global GHZ decoder are inherited. Consult related work before describing novelty.
- Finite numerical checks do not establish universal theorems, experimental performance, or publication priority.
- The common learning route has one educational anchor. Supplementary reviews in the bibliography are not additional prerequisites.
